approach.method_basis: Recover n-d88727c16484 with its algorithm unchanged: a task-local walk makes the fixed random atom, bond and ring edits from one scored current graph, filters invalid and canonically previously proposed molecules, and evaluates the first announced full batch allowed by tabu memory. A candidate is vetoed only when its signed radius-one motif changes match both inverse signs from the same active source transition. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph, even on worsening moves, with the existing canonical tie rule. The independent best archive, bounded balanced inverse-attribute installation, four-step tenure, latest-transition overlap refresh, oldest-first obstruction releases and passive allocation diagnostics all remain in place.
approach.novelty: This is implementation recovery, not a new search mechanism. Normalize the graph-edit result through the existing canonical_molecule helper before it supplies the pending identity and emitted SMILES. The repaired identity reflects the RDKit parse/serialize round trip that the recorded accepted feedback used; this repairs proposal-to-feedback matching without changing the bound same-transition bidirectional tabu mechanism.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-d88727c16484 completes seeds 0 and 1 but its seed-2 summary records a candidate early exit after 110 evaluations in zaleplon_mpo. Candidate stderr identifies RuntimeError: accepted_identity_has_no_current_neighbor_trace in Walk.observe. The first accepted molecule in batch 10 was stored and emitted as Cc1c(C(O)Cl)c(C)c2cc(C(=O)N3c4cccc3c4)oc2c1SN; the recorded feedback canonical_smiles is Cc1c(C(O)Cl)c(C)c2cc(C(=O)N3C4=CC=CC3=C4)oc2c1SN. apply_edit serializes the edited RDKit graph, then returns that string alongside a reparsed molecule whose aromatic representation has changed. The accepted-feedback lookup therefore cannot find the earlier spelling in pending. Replaying all ten recorded batches reproduces this exact exception, and replaying the single recorded close_ring edit isolates the identity mismatch.
hypothesis: Repair accepted-feedback trace lookup by using the canonical SMILES obtained after reparsing each generated edit, so proposal bookkeeping and returned molecular structure share the same identity used by the recorded feedback.

finding_summary.headline: The repaired walk completes all three seeds while preserving the recorded search behavior.
finding_summary.insights:
The new evidence closes the specific uncertainty left by the recovery run: the identity fix supports the full previously failing seed, beyond the ten batches that could be replayed earlier. Exact preservation of all available successful histories narrows the earlier interruption to proposal-to-feedback identity bookkeeping. The original executable has no completed continuation for the failed task, so this establishes operational recovery and a complete score estimate without establishing a new search advantage. The seed-0 comparison supplied with this replication is the same repaired algorithm, not a separate intervention.

The small spread in macro score also hides task variation: sitagliptin final scores range from 0.4484554129767839 to 0.5903526424693334 across the three seeds. The molecular assessment finds different ring frameworks across the added seeds but persistent reactive heteroatoms, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry, with late trajectories concentrated within related families. Successful identity handling and stable macro performance therefore leave chemical feasibility and useful scaffold coverage unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
The previously failing seed-2 feedback now reaches the correct pending proposal. The repaired walk processes all ten scores in that batch and continues to the full 300-evaluation task budget. Both added seeds complete all five tasks: 3,000 evaluations, 2,900 optimizer outcomes and 290 completed walk steps, with no invalid evaluations, duplicates or unresolved feedback. Replaying the original source still reproduces the exact identity-lookup exception, while the repaired replay matches the formal continuation.

The comparison preserves every one of the 4,310 previously recorded molecule/score entries in normalized order. All fourteen complete task logs are identical to the original runs; the failed prefix differs only in the spelling of one molecular identity, whose returned graph is unchanged. The inherited tabu behavior remains active in the two new seeds: 132 of 3,032 valid novel attempts are vetoed, while 1,577 partial inverse matches reach evaluation and supply 153 selected next states.

Macro final Top-1 is 0.518077929779343 for seed 0, 0.527798815337278 for seed 1 and 0.516876739241218 for seed 2. The complete three-seed mean is 0.5209178281192797, with population standard deviation 0.004890242222897396. The previously incomplete zaleplon task finishes at 0.41003927643747895. These are formal evaluation results; the diagnostic replay makes no oracle calls.

molecular.headline: Additional seeds vary the ring frameworks but retain reactive heteroatoms, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This report covers seeds 1 and 2 of n-9f7c7ec50039. The supplied parent comparison is the same node's existing seed-0 chemistry, not a new parent-to-child chemical intervention. All current tasks have 600 recorded entries and 580 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout; aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.719 to 1.0, and charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These counters describe SMILES-token presence, not aromatic atom fractions, basicity or stereochemical feasibility. The added seeds span recognizable indole/benzofuran amides, large nitrogen-rich diones, halogenated aromatic amine assemblies, bridged lactams and sulfur-rich cages. This gives moderate diversity across seeds and tasks, although each late trajectory remains concentrated in a related family. Several conventional medicinal fragments are retained, but many high-scoring complete structures have unusual sulfur valence, N-halogen or O-halogen bonds, highly constrained ring junctions or extensive flexible substitution. Rings and aromatic content are abundant; reliable synthetic accessibility and explicit stereochemistry remain the clearer gaps. The more conventional members should not be conflated with the implausible sulfur-rich and densely bridged leaders.

per_task.generated_character: Moderately sized aromatic carboxamides are prominent: seed 1 has ethoxy-, methyl- and thiol-substituted indole anilides, while seed 2 reaches an amino/chloro-substituted benzofuran N-chloroanilide. Later seed-2 molecules replace the fused aromatic core by bridged unsaturated oxygen or sulfur frameworks, retaining an aryl carbonyl-containing linkage. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9569 and halogen presence is 0.6552. The indole anilide is a comparatively plausible synthetic scaffold; chlorinated nitrogen, an aminochloromethyl centre and constrained sulfur cages are less convincing. Relative to the seed-0 aryl-ketone family, these seeds more often retain an amide among their best molecules.
liabilities: N-chloroamide, thiol and aminochloromethyl functionality adds reactivity to an otherwise recognizable aromatic scaffold.
Late bridged unsaturated sulfur structures and N-N linkages have unresolved geometry and synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: Broader accessible fused heteroaryl amides preserving the successful carbonyl and aromatic attachment pattern are poorly represented in the late output.
Defined stereochemical alternatives are absent for the aminochloromethyl centre and bridged ring junctions; the supplied molecules cannot establish a required stereoisomer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. A conventional substituted indole anilide reaches 0.39905049777278273, near the benzofuran N-chloroamide maximum of 0.41003927643747895. The latter exceeds the seed-0 maximum of 0.3966634883331815, but the visible chemistry does not show that its reactive groups are necessary. A distorted, partially saturated N-hydroxy heterocyclic amide scores only 0.030639811858172862. In a bridged family, chlorine and bromine analogues tie at 0.3900523103411983. Preserving a compact ring/carbonyl arrangement appears more consistently favorable than ring expansion or intricate heteroaryl replacement.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 family consists of large fused nitrogen-rich diones joined to a pyridine-containing oxygen/nitrogen ring system and a branched polyene side chain. It carries a mixed ketal, a butyl group, N-fluoromethyl and N-methylthiomethyl substituents. The fluorine in N-fluoromethyl is carbon-bound, not an N-F bond. Seed 1 instead explores expanded nitrogen heterocycles with imine, ester, alkyne and alkene substituents. All proposals contain aromatic and ring-closure tokens; mean SMILES length is 67.6, reflecting extensive substitution rather than directly measuring molecular size. Compared with the seed-0 best containing N-Br and unusual sulfur, the seed-2 leaders use more conventional valences, although their size, flexibility and mixed functionality remain problematic.
liabilities: Long polyenes, alkynes and mixed acetal functionality introduce isomerism, oxidation or hydrolysis concerns and complicate synthesis.
Large flexible substitution patterns and unspecified stereochemistry reduce confidence in a single accessible molecular shape.
missing_features: Compact versions preserving the recurring fused-dione and heteroaryl attachment pattern are underrepresented among the late high-scoring molecules.
Stable alternatives to the long unsaturated chains and mixed ketal/thioacetal-like substitution are not broadly explored at comparable core geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.548381482770623; a modified, strained fused imino/carbonyl structure scores 0.526081691583997. The expanded seed-2 dione family reaches 0.6092182584436399, below the seed-0 maximum of 0.6161710037174721. The best family tolerates different polyene termini, chlorine addition, and exchanging ketal oxygen substitution for sulfur at exactly 0.6092182584436399. Conversely, disrupting the fused dione with a sulfur-containing partially saturated ring gives 0.5548207448659938. The data favor retaining the heterocyclic arrangement while allowing substantial peripheral variation; they do not establish a single missing substituent.

per_task.generated_character: High-scoring seed-2 molecules combine a methylphenol ring and chlorophenyl group with cyclic tertiary nitrogen, aminomethyl substituents and fused unsaturated sulfur-containing rings. Seed 1 reaches a different rigid polyaryl framework with bromine, aniline, chloromethyl, a sulfur-bound hydroxyl group and a cumulated N=C=S linkage attached to a highly substituted sulfur centre. Aromatic presence is 1.0, halogen presence is 0.9948 and cumulated-double-bond token presence is 0.0879. These seeds replace the seed-0 aziridine-rich family by other aromatic/amine geometries, but retain unusual sulfur bonding and dense ring connectivity. Neutral SMILES do not establish the protonation state of the amines.
liabilities: Hydrogen-bearing multiply bonded sulfur, sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding and highly substituted cumulated systems raise strong stability and synthetic concerns.
Dense polycyclic geometry and heavily substituted aromatic surfaces combine with unspecified stereochemistry; a high score does not establish a feasible bound shape.
missing_features: Accessible cyclic-amine linkers preserving the favorable aromatic spacing without unusual multiply bonded sulfur remain underrepresented in the high-scoring output.
Defined configurations for substituted and fused saturated-ring centres are absent, and the trajectories do not compare chemically relevant protonation alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An early acid/amide/sulfonamide derivative scores 0.007468397818197266; the late phenol/amine/sulfur-ring family reaches 0.9148143511682032, compared with 0.8856242185485628 in seed 0. A related family with carbon versus sulfur at a ring position ties at 0.8825461379136246, despite a substantial chemical change. Removing a methylene in the amine-to-sulfur-ring connection gives 0.3331237338421948, and replacing the chlorophenyl partner by a sulfur-containing nonaromatic ring gives 0.04252669549740123. Aromatic placement and amine/linker geometry matter in the shown series, while the score alone does not resolve sulfur plausibility.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 produces bulky bridged nitrogen heterocycles with aromatic ether rings, lactam and ketone groups, an aryl ester, methoxy and alkyl substituents, and an N-N bond. Seed 1 instead explores brominated aryl lactam/carbamate families carrying thioesters and aryl O-Br, followed by more sulfur-rich variants. All proposals contain aromatic and ring-closure tokens; halogen presence is 0.4069. Relative to the smaller seed-0 bridged N-O family, these seeds have more extensive carbonyl, side-chain and ring substitution. Familiar aryl/carbonyl fragments are present, but the full bridged connectivity and reactive O-Br or unusual sulfur groups make apparent synthesis questionable.
liabilities: Aryl O-Br is a reactive hypobromite motif; thioesters and unusual sulfur centres add further stability questions.
Large bridged frameworks with multiple carbonyls and N-N bonds present unresolved ring geometry and substantial synthetic complexity.
missing_features: Less extensively bridged, synthetically accessible frameworks preserving the recurring aromatic and carbonyl arrangement are underrepresented among late molecules.
Stable realizations without aryl O-Br, unusual sulfur or unnecessary N-N connectivity are missing from much of the expanded family; stereochemical specification is absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329, an opened carbonyl-rich derivative scores 0.12467972074136988, and the best aryl-ether/bridged-dicarbonyl family reaches 0.20185639717998205. The seed-0 maximum was 0.2107445781802027. Retaining constrained aromatic/carbonyl geometry accompanies the higher scores; larger substitution alone gives no consistent gain. Replacing a bridge nitrogen by hydrogen-bearing sulfur leaves a matched pair at 0.1996542320706886. A late phenol-containing sulfur-rich analogue remains at 0.1881666776148033. The shallow gradient does not identify a unique missing target fragment or distinguish all chemically important heteroatom changes.

per_task.generated_character: Both seeds generate compact but densely interconnected sulfur/nitrogen cages. Seed-1 leaders retain a partially aromatic nitrogen-rich dione with NH, carbon-bound fluorine and a sulfur-linked fluorohydrin, surrounded by multiply bonded sulfur bridges. Seed-2 late products are nonaromatic cages containing ketone, aldehyde, N-fluoroamidine-like functionality and constrained sulfur/carbon unsaturation. Aromatic-token presence is 0.719 over both seeds, but the seed-2 final cages lack aromatic atoms in their displayed graphs. Compared with seed 0, the detailed functional groups and cage topology change substantially while unusual sulfur valence and unresolved stereochemistry persist. These are highly implausible complete synthetic targets despite recognizable carbonyl and nitrogen fragments.
liabilities: Multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur and crowded ring junctions raise severe chemical-stability and geometric-feasibility concerns.
Fluorohydrin, aldehyde and N-F functionality introduce further reactivity, while the cage stereochemistry is left unspecified.
missing_features: The sampled high-scoring region lacks a demonstrated accessible framework retaining the favorable carbonyl/nitrogen/fluorinated arrangement without unusual sulfur cages.
Stable alternatives to N-F and sulfur-linked fluorohydrin motifs, together with explicit bridge stereochemistry, are poorly represented in the late output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An early modified fused dione scores 7.590554525032884e-10 and an already sulfur-rich, N-fluorinated cage scores 1.0546805269255595e-09, so sulfur or fluorine presence alone is not predictive. The seed-1 dione/fluorohydrin cage reaches 0.5903526424693334 versus the seed-0 maximum of 0.48118636011729826. Seed 2 reaches 0.4484554129767839 in its final family. Related expanded ketone or lactone cage variants score 0.01685401516576383 and 0.2536619453071564, respectively. Scores are sensitive to detailed ring size, bond placement and carbonyl/nitrogen environment; the trajectories do not isolate a transferable target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest examples include N-chloroamides, N-F, aryl O-Br, multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds. Carbon/sulfur ring variants tie at 0.8825461379136246, and nitrogen/sulfur bridge variants tie at 0.1996542320706886 despite their different chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain stable heteroatom chemistry within favorable molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically conventional carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and ordinary sulfur alternatives while preserving attachment positions. General chemical feasibility must distinguish reactive or unusual bonding that the observed scalar feedback sometimes treats as equivalent.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest has ring-closure presence of 1.0 and stereocentre-token presence of 0.0. High-scoring structures include densely bridged sulfur cages, constrained lactams and substituted saturated ring junctions without explicit configurations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator creates elaborate ring closures without establishing accessible geometry or stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support accessible fused, spiro and less bridged alternatives, together with stereochemical assignment and variation where applicable. Preserve useful attachment geometry while distinguishing a valid molecular graph from a feasible stereochemical structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Large fused-dione products retain an identical score of 0.6092182584436399 after changing polyene termini, halogen substitution and ketal heteroatoms. Other late families retain bulky aryl/carbonyl frameworks while adding reactive sulfur or brominated substituents.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular growth and peripheral decoration dominate several late families without showing which additions are necessary.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make compact analogues and simpler linkers available alongside growth operations, preserving recurring aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements. Equivalent observed scores should permit exploration of structurally simpler and more conventional candidates.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied seeds reach different indole/benzofuran, fused-dione, aromatic-amine and cage structures, yet the high-scoring and final excerpts within each seed repeatedly vary one established framework. A conventional indole amide already reaches 0.39905049777278273, close to the more reactive neighboring family maximum of 0.41003927643747895.
transferable_gaps.gap: Diversity across seeds has not translated into broad accessible alternatives within each late chemical family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand scaffold and linker alternatives around chemically recognizable aromatic/carbonyl/amine patterns, including stable heterocycle replacements, rather than relying mainly on increasingly elaborate local heteroatom and ring changes.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
